title: Lord, Thou Wilt Hear Me When I Pray
description: Lord, Thou Wilt Hear Me When I Pray in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 4, part 2, headed “An evening Psalm”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, thou wilt hear me when I pray I am for ev-er thine: I fear be-fore thee all the day, Nor would I dare to sin.

lines: Lord, thou wilt hear me when I pray
I fear before thee all the day,
Nor would I dare to sin.
And while I rest my weary head
With my own heart and thee.
And when my work is done,
Great God, my faith and hope relies
Thus with my thoughts compos'd to peace
I'll give mine eyes to sleep;
Thy hand in safety keeps my days,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
